# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_GET_TRANSFERS::response_t, src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:1634-1649
#         -> FIVE lists: in, out, pending, failed, pool. Each is a list of transfer_entry.
#         transfer_entry = :1446-1487, all eighteen members KV_SERIALIZEd at :1468-1485:
#           txid string, payment_id string, height u64, timestamp u64, amount u64,
#           amounts[] = amounts_container = std::vector<uint64_t> (:1445 -- a BARE array of numbers,
#             not the { amounts: [...] } wrapper that single_transfer_response.amounts_by_dest uses),
#           fee u64, note string, destinations[] = transfer_destination (:474-482, {amount, address}),
#           type string, unlock_time u64, locked bool,
#           subaddr_index = cryptonote::subaddress_index (src/cryptonote_basic/subaddress_index.h:38-55),
#           subaddr_indices[] of the same, address string, double_spend_seen bool,
#           confirmations u64 (OPT, :1484), suggested_confirmations_threshold u64 (OPT, :1485)
# NO status/untrusted: the wallet RPC has no rpc_response_base.
#
# `type` HAS SIX VALUES, NOT FIVE, AND `block` LIVES IN THE `in` LIST. fill_transfer_entry types an
#   incoming row `pd.m_coinbase ? "block" : "in"` (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:501) and pushes
#   it into the `in` list, so "block" is an ordinary member of get_transfers' `in` array for any
#   wallet holding a mined or p2pool output. A five-variant TransferKind makes serde fail on the
#   WHOLE response, so `wallet history` exits 1 and the §2a.4 resolve step cannot complete -- which
#   under §2a.4's own rule leaves the pending record in place and blocks every later send. Row 3
#   below is that row, and it is the reason this file exists in DESIGN.md §8's list.
#
# `subaddr_index` IS AN OBJECT, NOT A NUMBER: {"major": N, "minor": M}
#   (subaddress_index.h:51-54). `major` IS the account index, so §5b's Transfer carries a
#   SubaddrIndex and has no separate account_index field. A u32 there fails to deserialize every row.
#
# `confirmations` AND `locked` ARE DERIVED PER RESPONSE, NOT STORED, AND AGAINST THE WALLET'S HEIGHT.
#   wallet-rpc recomputes them on every call from m_wallet->get_blockchain_current_height()
#   (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:162, called at :505, :535, :566, :589). The values below are
#   computed for wh = 3541122, which is wallet/get_height.json -- NOT node/get_info.json's height,
#   even though the two coincide in this fixture set. §5b's history cache stores NEITHER field.
#     confirmations = 0 when height == 0 or height >= wh, else wh - height
#     locked        = !(age_ok && spendtime_ok), TWO INDEPENDENT CONDITIONS (wallet2.cpp:7308-7344),
#                     not a maximum:
#       age_ok       = height != 0 && height + 10 <= wh        (SPENDABLE_AGE, cryptonote_config.h:49)
#       spendtime_ok = unlock_time == 0                                  -> true
#                      unlock_time <  500000000 (CRYPTONOTE_MAX_BLOCK_NUMBER, :40) -> wh >= unlock_time
#                      otherwise (a UNIX TIMESTAMP)                      -> adjusted_now + 120 >= unlock_time
#     unlock_time IS NEVER A DELTA ADDED TO height. Rows 3 and 4 are the two branches.
#   pending and pool rows are UNCONDITIONALLY locked (:551, :581) regardless of the formula.
#
# THE ROWS, and what each one is for:
#   in[0]   plain confirmed incoming. unlock_time 0, so spendtime_ok is the trivial branch.
#           confirmations = 3541122 - 3540000 = 1122; age_ok true; locked false.
#   in[1]   THE TIMESTAMP BRANCH. unlock_time 1900000000 is >= 500000000, so it is a unix timestamp
#           (2030-03-17), not a height. adjusted_now (1789560131 in this fixture set) + 120 is far
#           below it, so locked is TRUE even though age_ok is true and confirmations is 3122. Treating
#           unlock_time as a delta on height would mark this unlocked; treating it as a height would
#           read it as block 1.9 billion and mark every such row locked until the year 55000.
#           DESIGN.md §8's Phase 1b gate names this exact value.
#   in[2]   THE COINBASE ROW, type "block", inside the `in` list. unlock_time 3539060 = height + 60
#           (CRYPTONOTE_MINED_MONEY_UNLOCK_WINDOW, cryptonote_config.h:44) and is an ABSOLUTE HEIGHT,
#           so the height branch applies: wh 3541122 >= 3539060, spendtime_ok true, locked false.
#           A second coinbase-specific 60-block rule would double-count that window (§1b.4).
#   out[0]  confirmed outgoing, with a NON-EMPTY destinations[] -- the one fact a user checks after a
#           send, which is why §5b's Transfer carries the field and §7a's detail pane renders it.
#           Carries a `note`, so set_tx_notes/get_tx_notes have something to round-trip.
#   pending[0] height 0, confirmations 0, locked true. ITS txid IS transfer-do-not-relay.json's
#           tx_hash, relay_tx.json's tx_hash and get_transfer_by_txid.json's transfer.txid -- so the
#           §2a.4 resolve step finds the transaction a build-then-relay just broadcast, which is what
#           makes a normal successful send leave nothing behind.
#   failed[0] height 0, locked true. A row the wallet saw that did not make it. §2a.4 counts `failed`
#           as FOUND, so this row must exist for the "record self-clears" test to be writable.
#   pool[0] height 0, locked true. The `pool` list is the ONLY one whose branch runs
#           update_pool_state/process_pool_state -- a daemon round trip (:2939-2950) -- which is why
#           history::query sends `pool: true` only when asked (§1b.4, §4.1).
#
# `amounts[]` is populated only where the wallet recorded per-destination amounts; upstream leaves it
#   empty on rows it did not split, and both shapes appear below.
# `payment_id` is 16 zeros for a payment with no id -- pod_to_hex of a null crypto::hash8 -- not an
#   empty string and not null. An integrated address would put a real 16-hex id here.
# `suggested_confirmations_threshold` is on the wire but §5b's Transfer does not carry it; it is
#   derived per response like confirmations and is not a field fmonero reads.
# addresses are real, checksum-valid mainnet vectors from upstream's own test suite:
#   our own:     validate_address.py:68 (standard, prefix 18), :73 and :74 (subaddress, prefix 42)
#   counterparty: validate_address.py:69 (standard, prefix 18)
# request: DESIGN.md §1b.4 -- `filter_by_height` is NOT KV_SERIALIZE_OPT (:1624), so an omitted flag
#   value-initialises to false and min_height/max_height are silently ignored (:2890-2895). A fixture
#   mock cannot catch that (it serves this same file either way), which is why the flag is a field of
#   the frozen TransferQuery type and the assertion is made on the --log file's recorded request.
